elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1: "each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed..." — the cap is expressed per Party, so it binds Vendor and Customer alike, and no residual language leaves Customer uncapped.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1: "the greater of fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000." Basis (paid or payable, not the narrower "actually paid"), lookback anchor (preceding the claim) and the USD 1,000,000 floor all match. Note the lower-case "fees" reads as the generic term rather than the narrow §1.5 defined "Fees", which is directionally consistent with the playbook base.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 21.2: "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill" — already mutual and untouched.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.1 now opens "Except for Excluded Claims," and 21.3 defines Excluded Claims to include "a Party's breach of confidentiality... obligations"; the prior "without exception" override that had defeated 21.3 is deleted.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "data-protection, or security obligations", now effective against the cap via the reinstated "Except for Excluded Claims" carve-out in 21.1.
21.3 includes "its indemnification obligations" within Excluded Claims, which sit outside the 21.1 cap.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" are Excluded Claims and therefore outside the 21.1 cap.
21.3 expressly lists "wilful misconduct" among Excluded Claims; 21.1 excepts Excluded Claims from the cap.
21.3 expressly lists "fraud" among Excluded Claims, now carved out of the cap by the amended 21.1.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim and thus uncapped under amended 21.1.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Amended 21.3: "Customer's obligation to pay amounts due under this Agreement is not damages and is not limited by this Section." This cures the prior reliance on the narrow §1.5 "Fees" definition (excluding taxes, expenses and implementation charges), so the carve-out now reaches Customer payment obligations as a whole.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1 caps "each Party's aggregate liability"; no one-sided or unlimited-Customer language remains.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1 uses "fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim" (with a USD 1,000,000 floor), replacing the one-month base.
"Except for Excluded Claims" in 21.1 plus 21.3's inclusion of "its indemnification obligations".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes breach of confidentiality obligations, now effective because "without exception" was removed from 21.1.
21.3 lists gross negligence as an Excluded Claim outside the 21.1 cap.
21.3 lists wilful misconduct as an Excluded Claim outside the 21.1 cap.

reasons: Finding status "deviation" is correct: original 21.1 capped both Parties at one month of "Fees actually paid" — below the 6-month walk-away floor — and "without exception" nullified the Excluded Claims regime, placing indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap with no super-cap.

Preferred level is complete: mutual cap, greater-of twelve months' fees paid or payable measured to the claim plus USD 1,000,000 floor, retained mutual consequential-damages exclusion in 21.2, the full 21.3 Excluded Claims list operative again, and a payment carve-out reaching Customer's payment obligations generally.

Minimality holds: only two surgical edits were made — replacing the cap basis and the "without exception" override in 21.1, and replacing the narrow "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" noun phrase in 21.3. The latter is required by the checklist element, since §1.5 "Fees" excludes taxes, expenses and implementation charges and so covers only a subset of Customer's payment obligations. No survival tails, procedures, expense language or extra damages categories were added, and 21.2 was left untouched.

Watch-item (not a failure): the amended 21.3 also drops the "undisputed" and "conforming Services" qualifiers, which were Customer-favourable limits on an uncapped Customer payment exposure. The element could be met by a narrower edit such as "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed amounts due under this Agreement for conforming Services"; the margin comment already offers to restore those qualifiers, which is the safer negotiating stance.

Intent preserved: 21.2's cross-reference to "Excluded Claims" and 21.3's definition remain coherent, the direct-damages sentence in 21.2 survives, and no undefined term or dangling reference is created (lower-case "fees" in 21.1 reads as the generic term and is the playbook's own formulation, though the drafter may confirm the intended base with the counterparty).
